The email identifier shares one budget per account\n  // across IPs — distributed credential stuffing cannot rotate around it.\n  @RateLimit({\n    name: 'login',\n    limit: 5,\n    windowMs: 15 * 60_000,\n    identifier: ({ args }) =>\n      ((args?.['input'] as { email?: string } | undefined)?.email ?? '').toLowerCase() ||\n      undefined,\n  })\n  @Public()\n  @Mutation(() => AuthPayload)\n  async login(\n    @Args('input') input: LoginInput,\n    @Context() context: GqlContext,\n  ): Promise<AuthPayload> {\n    // PERF-MEDIUM-003: tier-0 login latency SLI. A registry whose entry can be minted by the reviewed party is not a registry. The allowlist arm is also matched per FILE (security-boundary-adapter.ts:210 fires only when the unit is unlisted), so registering this endpoint would silence every present and future endpoint in mfa.resolver.ts.\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"case\": \"TP-B: the adapter cannot see inside MfaService, so flagging an unguarded token-issuing mutation is a correct alarm awaiting human triage.\",\n          \"why_it_fails\": \"The alarm's discriminator does not track the hazard. verifyMfaLogin's boundary is the signed challenge token plus the per-mfaToken velocity limit at mfa.resolver.ts:251, which caps guesses against a six-digit space at five per login session; the endpoint is public by construction because the caller has no session yet (mfa.resolver.ts:260).
